steps.note: S1.3.1.1 says rows 0-1 subtract Ja+Rc, rows 2-5 add R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx), rows 6-7 restore a,c, so the target changes by (JV+RG)x whatever a,c are, matching the paper.
S1.3.1.2 gives central coefficient |S∩T| mod 2, side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, zero for intersections 0 or 2, and self coefficient one.
S1.3.1.3 gives central coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2, side wires cancelling distinct triples meeting in 0 or 2 points, and self coefficient (3-1)/2=1.
S1.3.1.4 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) from the inverse schedule X<-X-Y and that each invocation restores its own auxiliary wires.

The plan states that every edge joins comparable labels (S1.3.3, S1.3.3.4) but never gives the per-edge orthogonal residuals or their dimensions (no residual table, no B/P/F tensor splitting); S1.3.3.6 only defines a residual.

S1.3.3.3 gives <t_X> inside t_Y^perp because t_X is orthogonal to t_Y, but not the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2 (the h-2 appears nowhere in the plan), and it is stated for a generic side wire (quote from line 953), not as the 2->5 residual.
S1.3.3.4 gives center 3->4 as the only decreasing edge losing h; S1.3.3.2 gives source sum N and sink sum Wm-N; S1.3.3.5 telescopes to signed Wm-2N and adds 2L for absolute changes.

S1.3.3.6 states that over F_2 every nonzero residual has a norm-one vector, hence is nondegenerate and nonalternating, hence has an orthonormal basis; the plan does not spell out the absorption of alternating planes, but the claim and its reason are stated.
S1.3.3.7 states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.
S1.3.5.1 gives wt(z+w)=wt(z)+wt(w)-2|supp∩supp|, additivity mod 4 for z.w=0, and q_V-q_U as a sum of wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal basis of the residual.
S1.3.5.2 says each basis vector has odd weight, the phase is i^{±[v.x]} expanded as (1+i^±)/2+(1-i^±)/2 (-1)^{v.x}, and H diag(1,-1) H = X gives aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The plan never mentions k columns or tensoring the edge operator over columns; it gives one kernel per residual basis vector and the total s_c (S1.3.5, S1.3.5.3) but not the per-column tensored-factor statement.

The plan does not state the endpoint frames (zero label I, full label C^{⊗m}) or that X_a->Y_a carries C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a); S1.5.1.5 only names 'source and sink Z signs, the scalar i^{27f} and negation of the X bank' and S1.5.1.3 gives (C^{-1})^{⊗f}=(-i)^f Z C Z without the endpoint derivation.
The plan gives L/N<1/2 (S1.3.3, S1.3.3.7), the deficit N-2L_b>0 with s_b<W_b m (S1.3.4.3), and the deficit 2N-2L_c>0 for the complex count (S1.3.5.3).

S1.3.6 states both deficits exceed 20·2^-50, log m<20 from m<2^20, so m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20·2^-50), hence s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma=1-2^-50 (the intermediate '>m(1-eta)' step is implicit).
S1.3.7.1 describes elimination from the topmost nonzero row with its rightmost pivot using only lower-triangular operations, one rank-one block per step, giving A=E1 Pi E2 with exactly a ones in Pi.

S1.3.7 only says in its claim that q is a fixed odd prime avoiding all denominators; the plan does not state the finite table of factors or that the identities specialize to Z/q^b with the triangular factors staying invertible, so I treat it as named without its content.

S1.3.7.2 says a lower-triangular transformation of H or D costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order, each by a unit multiple plus a fixed combination of earlier unchanged coordinates.
S1.3.7.3 realizes each one of Pi as D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange of (H_i,D_j), and D_j<-H_i-D_j, one interchange per one, exactly a in all.
